title: Best Auto-Apply Tools for Remote Entry-Level Tech Jobs in 2026
summary: Compare auto-apply tools for remote entry-level tech roles, including supported-system submission, tailoring, review controls, and receipts.
body_markdown:
Remote entry-level tech roles can attract large applicant pools soon after they go live. New grads, bootcamp graduates, and recent CS majors may be competing across the same Workday, Greenhouse, and Lever postings, and a prompt application can enter an earlier review batch. Auto-apply tools promise to close that speed gap, but the category is uneven. Some are Chrome autofillers dressed up as agents, some cap you at LinkedIn-style applications, and a few actually submit end-to-end on real employer systems. This guide walks through what to look for, compares the leading options, and explains why[Tsenta](https://tsenta.com/) ranks #1 for new grads targeting remote entry-level tech roles in 2026.


## Why Auto-Apply Tools Matter for Remote Entry-Level Tech Roles


Remote entry-level tech postings can be highly competitive, but applicant counts and review practices vary widely by employer and role. For a new grad without a strong referral network, consistent targeting and prompt applications are two practical levers. Manual applying also takes time once you factor in account creation, form fields, and screening questions. Auto-apply tools can reduce that repetitive work.


### Problems New Grads Face When Applying to Remote Tech Roles


- **Volume ceiling.** Manual applications limit how many relevant roles most people can cover in a day.
- **Latency.** Tools that batch applications infrequently can add avoidable delay on fresh postings.
- **ATS fragmentation.** Remote tech roles live on Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, iCIMS, and other systems, and support varies by tool.
- **Filter fatigue.** New grads waste hours filtering out senior-only roles, on-site roles, and postings that quietly require work authorization.


Auto-apply tools address these problems by watching career pages, tailoring materials per role, and submitting through supported employer systems. Tsenta focuses specifically on the end-to-end submission piece, which is what actually gets a new grad into the early applicant pool.


## What to Look for in an Auto-Apply Tool for Remote Entry-Level Tech Jobs


Not every tool that claims "auto-apply" actually submits an application. Many are autofill extensions that fill fields but still require you to click submit on every posting. For new grads targeting remote roles at scale, the differences matter.


### Features That Actually Move the Needle


- **True end-to-end submission on real employer systems.** The tool should log in, complete the full form, answer open-ended questions in your voice, upload documents, and submit, not just autofill your name.
- **Broad ATS coverage.** Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, iCIMS, and similar systems are common employer hiring platforms.
- **Per-role résumé and cover-letter preparation.** Initial résumé reviews can be brief, so relevance signals need to be easy to see.
- **a receipt for every successful submission.** You should be able to see exactly what was sent.
- **Filtering for remote and entry-level.** Signals for location, seniority, and work-authorization preferences should be first-class filters.
- **Fast turnaround.** A prompt application may enter an earlier review batch.
- **Honest, published pricing.** No hidden credit-pack mazes or add-ons for basic functionality.


Tsenta is designed against this checklist directly. It surfaces relevant roles, prepares job-specific materials from your saved candidate context, and submits complete applications on supported employer systems including Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, and others, with an inspectable receipt for every successful submission.


## How New Grads Are Using Auto-Apply Tools to Land Remote Tech Roles


The most effective new-grad workflows in 2026 combine an auto-apply agent with a light human review loop. A CS senior graduating in December might set up candidate context such as a résumé, projects, work-authorization answers, and a remote-only filter, then use the agent while finishing coursework. When a matching remote SWE role appears on Greenhouse or Workday, the agent prepares the materials and submits, and the receipt lands in the tracker.


**Common strategies:**


- **Strategy 1: Volume with quality controls.** Cast a wide net across supported systems, but keep review controls on for higher-signal roles.
- **Strategy 2: Tight filtering for remote entry-level.** Use role-level filters (remote, 0 to 2 years, tech) so the agent only submits to genuinely relevant postings.
- **Strategy 3: Multi-surface access.** Approve matches from mobile between classes or interviews. Tsenta's iOS and Android apps are live.
- **Strategy 4: Layer a tracker.** Auto-apply tools submit, but a tracker helps you follow up manually on the roles that respond.


Tsenta is built for this workflow. It runs continuously, prepares tailored materials, and gives you a receipt for every successful submission so you always know what was sent.

### 2. LazyApply


[LazyApply](https://lazyapply.com/) is one of the earlier volume-focused auto-apply tools. It is a browser-based automation tool, delivered as a Chrome extension, that works through supported job application forms within daily limits.


**Key Features:** Browser-based automation, profile-driven autofill, daily submission caps, tracking dashboard.


**Remote Entry-Level Tech Offerings:** Bulk applying on LinkedIn, Indeed, and ZipRecruiter postings that include remote entry-level tech roles.


**Pricing:** As of August 2026,[LazyApply's public pricing](https://lazyapply.com/) lists Basic at $99 per year with 15 applications per day, Premium at $149 per year with 150 applications per day, and Ultimate at $999 per year with 1,500 applications per day.


**Pros:**


- Low annual entry price for volume-first applicants.
- Simple flat pricing with no per-application charges.
- Handles LinkedIn-style forms reliably.


**Cons:**


- Coverage is centered on LinkedIn, Indeed, ZipRecruiter, and Glassdoor, which misses many remote tech roles hosted on Workday, Greenhouse, and Lever career pages.
- Annual billing up front with no monthly option.
- Volume-first design produces less-tailored submissions.


### 3. JobCopilot


[JobCopilot](https://jobcopilot.com/pricing/) is a career-page-focused auto-apply service with review options. The vendor says it connects to more than 500,000 verified company career pages, and after setup, a copilot finds relevant jobs and can automate applications.


**Key Features:** Daily match feed, review-before-submit mode, AI résumé and cover-letter generation, application tracker.


**Remote Entry-Level Tech Offerings:** Career-page auto-apply with filters for remote and entry-level roles.


**Pricing:** As of August 2026,[JobCopilot's pricing page](https://jobcopilot.com/pricing/) lists Premium from $0.93 per day and Elite from $1.05 per day, with weekly, monthly, and quarterly plans available.


**Pros:**


- Focuses on verified company career pages.
- Daily match feeds keep the workflow structured.
- Review-first mode gives users more control.


**Cons:**


- Its daily-rate presentation takes extra work to compare with flat monthly plans.
- Daily match allowances depend on the plan and are not guaranteed completed applications.


### 4. AIApply


AIApply markets a broad AI job-search suite with an auto-apply add-on. Beyond auto-applying, AIApply offers tools like Interview Buddy for live interview coaching, AI mock interviews, a resume scanner, a job board, and an application tracker.


**Key Features:** Interview prep tools, résumé builder, job board, auto-apply add-on.


**Remote Entry-Level Tech Offerings:** Criteria-based matching with Auto Apply purchased as credits.


**Pricing:** As of August 2026,[AIApply's Auto Apply guide](https://support.aiapply.co/en/articles/14216708-how-does-auto-apply-work) lists $49 per month for 100 applications, $99 per month for 250, or $199 per quarter for 750. The toolkit and tailoring add-ons are priced separately.


**Pros:**


- Strong interview-prep tools bundled in.
- Broad feature set for a single suite.
- Working résumé and cover-letter generation.


**Cons:**


- Auto Apply is priced separately from the Premium toolkit.
- Tailored résumé and cover-letter add-ons increase the total cost.


### 5. LoopCV


[LoopCV](https://www.loopcv.pro/pricing/) is an auto-apply platform that matches users to roles and submits across supported workflows on more than 30 job boards.


**Key Features:** Job board integrations, match-based apply, résumé tailoring, recruiter outreach.


**Remote Entry-Level Tech Offerings:** Cross-board auto-apply with match filters for remote and entry-level roles.


**Pricing:** Free tier available; paid plans vary. Verify current tiers on LoopCV's pricing page.


**Pros:**


- Free plan to test match quality before paying.
- Broad job-board coverage.
- Match-first workflow.


**Cons:**


- Board-focused coverage means less depth on direct-career-page systems like Workday and Ashby.
- Match quality depends heavily on how tightly filters are configured.


### 6. Simplify


Simplify is one of the most widely installed job-search extensions in the category, but it is an autofill tool rather than an auto-apply agent. Simplify is a free Chrome autofill extension (the "Copilot") that fills job-application forms across major ATS like Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby and Workday, plus a job board and tracker. It is not true auto-apply: you still click Submit on every application.


**Key Features:** Autofill across 100+ ATS platforms, job tracker, curated matches, paid Simplify+ tier for tailored materials.


**Remote Entry-Level Tech Offerings:** Fast autofill on remote tech postings hosted on major ATS systems.


**Pricing:** As of August 2026,[Simplify's help center](https://help.simplify.jobs/en/help/articles/5623502-whats-included-in-simplify-features-and-pricing) lists a free core tier and Simplify+ at $19.99 per week, $39.99 per month, or $89.99 for three months.


**Pros:**


- Excellent free autofill experience on major ATS.
- Solid built-in tracker.


**Cons:**


- Does not submit for you, which caps the volume advantage.
- AI features (tailored resume writing, cover letter generation, custom Q&A answers for applications) require Simplify+ at $39.99/month.
- Paid AI features require a separate Simplify+ subscription.


### 7. Sorce


[Sorce](https://www.sorce.jobs/articles/sorce-pricing) is a mobile-first auto-apply tool with a swipe-style interface. Its public pricing page lists 40 free swipes per day with AI auto-apply on iOS.


**Key Features:** Mobile-first swipe interface, iOS and web access, daily free cap.


**Remote Entry-Level Tech Offerings:** Mobile approvals for remote tech roles surfaced through the match feed.


**Pricing:** 40 free swipes per day as of August 2026, with paid tiers for higher volume.


**Pros:**


- Generous free-tier daily cap on iOS.
- Fast, mobile-native approval flow.
- Low friction to try.


**Cons:**


- Narrower ATS coverage than agents built around Workday and other enterprise systems.
- Mobile-first design can limit the depth of review for complex roles.


## Evaluation Rubric for Auto-Apply Tools for Remote Entry-Level Tech Jobs


New grads should weight the following categories when picking an auto-apply tool. The percentages reflect how much each dimension typically matters for someone targeting remote entry-level tech roles at volume.


- **End-to-end submission capability (30%):** Does the tool actually submit, or just autofill?
- **Employer-system coverage (25%):** How well does it handle Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, iCIMS, and similar systems?
- **Material quality (15%):** Are résumés and cover letters prepared per role from your real background?
- **Transparency and receipts (10%):** Can you inspect what was sent?
- **Pricing honesty (10%):** Is pricing published, predictable, and free of add-on mazes?
- **Filtering for remote and entry-level (10%):** Can you constrain the agent to the roles you actually want?
